## Description

<!-- SECTION:DESCRIPTION:BEGIN -->
opum-agent's release-gate investigation (2026-09-02) found that lore check with no argument and lore check . behave very differently from the same directory. From opum-doc's repo root: lore check (no arg) reports 134 files / 0 errors / 0 warnings / 92 out-of-bundle links skipped. lore check . reports 555 files / 14 errors / 567 warnings / 0 skipped, with 246 output lines referencing .herdr/, a gitignored 1.2 GB vendored toolchain the docs bundle does not own. Reproduced identically on installed 0.3.5 and on dev HEAD, so this is not a 0.4.0 regression -- it predates that release and has been latent for months. A docs gate that fails on files the project never wrote, purely because the invocation had an explicit path argument, is the same class of silent-wrong as LCLI-377: nobody notices until it fires. Two things to establish during investigation rather than assume: (1) the two symptoms (gitignore-aware scoping, and out-of-bundle-link skip count) may not share one cause -- treat them as two code paths until proven otherwise; (2) the correct behavior is a design question, not an obvious bug fix -- an explicit path argument could legitimately mean 'check exactly this directory, ignoring gitignore', in which case the defect is that lore does not say so (docs/help text), not that it scopes differently. Do not assume the fix is 'make the explicit-path case match the no-arg case' without deciding that question first.
<!-- SECTION:DESCRIPTION:END -->

- [ ] #2 A decision is recorded on the task for what the correct behavior of an explicit path argument should be (match the no-arg path's gitignore-aware scoping, or intentionally check exactly the given path and document that loudly), before any code changes
- [ ] #3 Fix (or documentation fix, per the decision above) implemented and covered by a regression test reproducing the opum-doc symptom shape (a docs root containing a large gitignored non-bundle directory)

implementationNotes:
ROOT CAUSE (AC1), verified by reading the source, not assumed: there are NOT two diverging code paths. `collectBundles` (check.ts) resolves roots as `paths.length > 0 ? paths : [DOCS_DIR]` and both cases feed the identical `expandRoot` -> `walkFiles` walk. Neither the no-arg case nor the explicit-path case had ANY gitignore-awareness before this fix -- `walkFiles`/`walkMarkdown` (core/bundle.ts) recurse into every real subdirectory unconditionally, skipping only symlinks and unreadable directories. The opum-doc symptom (134/0/0/92 with no arg vs 555/14/567/0 with ".") is fully explained by which directory got walked (docs/, which never contained .herdr/, vs the repo root, which does), not by any divergence in gitignore handling between the two invocation styles -- there was no gitignore handling in either.

DECISION (AC2), recorded before any code change: `lore check` gains real gitignore-awareness, applied uniformly to both the no-arg default and any explicit path (never a special case for one or the other), rather than "intentionally check exactly the given path and document the difference." Reasoning: a docs gate exploding on files the project's own .gitignore says don't matter is a defect regardless of whether the path was implicit or explicit -- the same class of silent-wrong LCLI-377 named. Implementation: `git ls-files --others --ignored --exclude-standard --directory`, run synchronously (mirrors this codebase's existing adapters/git.ts Bun.spawnSync pattern) with `cwd` set to the bundle root being walked, reusing git's own canonical ignore engine instead of hand-rolling gitignore semantics or adding a parsing dependency. `--directory` collapses a wholly-ignored directory to one entry so the walk can prune it BEFORE descending (the .herdr/-shaped case), while an individually-ignored file inside an otherwise-tracked directory (this repo's own docs/.obsidian/*.json) is filtered out of the final file list. Fails open (returns null, no filtering) when the root is not inside a git repository or git is unavailable -- gitignore-awareness is advisory, never a hard requirement, so `lore check` still works outside git.

FIX (AC3): `core/bundle.ts`'s `walkFiles` gains an optional `skipDir` pruning predicate (default: never prunes, so `walkMarkdown` and every other existing caller is untouched). `commands/check.ts`'s `expandRoot` computes the ignored-entry set via the new `gitIgnoredEntries` and passes a directory-pruning predicate plus a post-walk file filter. Three new regression tests in check.test.ts reproduce the opum-doc symptom shape directly: a git-ignored vendor/ directory (with nested content) inside an explicitly-checked root produces zero findings and the no-arg/explicit-path skip counts now agree for the same bundle scope; an individually-ignored file inside docs/ is also excluded; and a non-git root falls back to the original unfiltered walk without failing `lore check`.

VERIFIED LIVE against this repo's own real gitignored content (not just the test fixtures): `bun run src/cli.ts check .` went from 587 files / 253 errors / 1816 warnings (walking node_modules/, .repro-scratch/, evals/results/, etc.) to 238 files / 1 error / 24 warnings -- the one remaining error is `test/fixtures/okf-bundle/broken/dangling-link.md`, a real, tracked, deliberately-broken fixture unrelated to gitignore.

AC4: the no-arg and explicit-path invocations now report the SAME skip count for the same conceptual bundle scope (proven in the new regression test), because gitignore filtering applies identically to both -- satisfied by making them consistent, not by documenting a divergence.

Full suite: 2877 pass (3 new), 1 skip (pre-existing), 0 fail. typecheck clean; lint exit 0 (one pre-existing unrelated warning). lore check: 77 files, 0 errors, 0 warnings.
